description: We are NAA, we are space explorants. We create apps based on demand and interests of fellow friends.
summary: Our game "Mars, Last Colony" uses captivating and educational gameplay to teach users how to plan, and structure a NASA space mission, how to land a shuttle on Mars, and how to sustain life on Mars. Throughout the game, players are met with challenges and decisions that impact the future of their colony. The astronaut can experience mars in different environmental structures, e.g. icy - rich plains. Our project addresses the challenge by captivating the user into a real life mars survival simulation: surviving on limited resources, building a colony and making important engineering decisions. We believe the creation of our mars game is important to educate the younger generation about mars and the data we have discovered from there through a fun, educational, and interesting game.
details:
"Mars, Last Colony" is a free, browser-based educational game that teaches players how NASA plans a space mission, lands on Mars and sustains life there. It follows three stages. In the Mission Design Lab, players follow NASA’s own process: they choose a science goal, compare spacecraft, fit instruments within a payload limit, pick a real rocket, and find an Earth–Mars launch window calculated from JPL planet positions. Every choice appears in 3D, and each mission is scored, compared with real NASA missions and saved. Next, players fly the landing themselves from a cockpit with a live LIDAR scan. Finally, they run a colony at one of five sites inspired by real places on Mars. They balance oxygen, water, food and power, repair failing systems, research technology and complete six missions while surviving dust storms and marsquakes.

The game turns abstract trade-offs into decisions players can feel: heavier instruments need bigger rockets, and solar power fails in dust storms. It runs on any computer or phone with nothing to install, and 34 real NASA facts appear when they matter. Our intended impact is to give students of every level a hands-on understanding of real mission design and inspire them to pursue space science.

Our team designed the game, and Claude, Anthropic’s AI, made it through Claude Code using JavaScript, HTML and CSS for the game, Three.js for the 3D graphics, PeerJS for four-player co-op, Supabase for accounts, GitHub for the code and Vercel for hosting. The science comes from NASA and JPL data and results from missions such as Perseverance, Curiosity, InSight and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

It is creative because players live with the consequences of the mission they planned. We balanced accuracy with simplicity: estimates are labelled, fiction is stated clearly, and every fact is sourced. We also designed for accessibility and teamwork.
